Subject: Questions about output ownership and training use in MSA/Order Form

Hi Dylan —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Procurement and legal ran a quick pass on the draft order form and MSA and flagged a couple of items that will block sign-off unless we land on language:

1) Output ownership: altum wants an explicit assignment (or at least exclusive rights) to productized outputs and derivative features when we deploy models trained on our data.
2) Training use: we need a deterministic opt-out for training on customer data, plus a requirement that if Redwood uses feedback to improve models, we get notice and a 12-month sunset on any feedback license.
3) Telemetry/evidence: procurement needs an evidence checklist (what logs/audit artifacts Redwood will supply) to satisfy our security review.

I attached our redlines (altum_redlines_marked.pdf) — can you confirm what tradeoffs Redwood can accept? Also, we have a tight procurement window (aiming to sign the week of 11/20).

Regards,
Sam Chen
Head of Product Ops | Altum AI

Dylan / Laura —

High-level counterproposals we can present to Altum that are reasonably low-risk operationally:

A) Output rights: Offer a nonexclusive, perpetual, worldwide license to use, reproduce, and distribute outputs for Altum's product(s). If Altum wants assignment for a narrow class of \"productized features\" we can carve that out but require additional fees and an escrow holdback for 6 months to cover model rollback/defect remediation.

B) Training opt-out: Add a per-orderform boolean (checkbox) that disables Redwood's use of Altum-provided prompts/data for model training/weight updates. Default is opt-in; customers can request opt-out which requires a 30-day operational lead to apply to model training pipelines.

C) Feedback license: Limit to a 12-month royalty-free license for aggregated, deidentified improvements (no attribution), with a contractual notice requirement and option to terminate on breach.

D) Evidence: Provide a standard evidence bundle: (1) token-level request logs (anonymized), (2) KV cache access logs for relevant time windows, (3) SOC 2 report and summary of retention windows. We should be clear about redactions and PSP/PII handling.

I'll draft suggested language for A/B/C. If legal signs off, we can send a marked MSA and Order Form back to Altum.

-Ben

Dylan / Ben —

Uploading redline language for Section 6 (Output & Training) — see attached: MSA_Sec6_output_redline.docx. Summary of our position:

- We will not assign model weights or grant exclusive ownership of the underlying model artifacts.
- We will provide an exclusive-like commercial pathway by granting a tailored, exclusive right to productize \"Deliverables\" specifically defined in the Order Form, conditioned on payment of Productization Fee (orderform).
- Training opt-out will be available per-order with a 30-day operational lag. We propose the opt-out be recorded as a checkbox in the Order Form and reflected in an exhibit that enumerates what data is excluded.
- Feedback license: language limits Redwood to using deidentified, aggregated feedback for internal model safety and tooling improvements for up to 12 months; any commercial re-use beyond that requires separate agreement.
- Evidence bundle: we can supply the items Ben suggested. Note we must mark any logs that contain customer PII as \"redacted\" and we will provide a summary attestation of the redaction approach.

If that matches product and GTM tolerances, I can produce a clean marked MSA + Order Form to send back. Legal note: Productization Fee and escrow holdback must be approved by Finance for any assignment-like rights.

Laura Bennett
Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference

Dylan / Team —

Thank you — the proposed approach is workable with a couple of small asks before we sign:

1) Training opt-out: Altum requires the opt-out to be effective immediately for any customer-provided training datasets if the customer selects it prior to first data ingestion. If a 30-day operational lag is unavoidable, we need a written interim guarantee that Redwood will not use our data for any published model updates until the opt-out window completes.

2) Productization Fee: Altum can agree to a Productization Fee structure but asks for a single-year price cap and a right of first negotiation on subsequent model versions derived from Altum data.

3) Feedback license sunset: please confirm the 12-month sunset is firm and that any aggregated improvements used in models will not be retrainable on our raw prompts without separate consent.

If we can get the above in the marked MSA and an evidence checklist (sample artifacts) we will route to procurement and aim to countersign via DocuSign.

DocuSign preview: https://www.docusign.com/altum_orderform_10293

Sam Chen
